programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: A programme of remarkable debuts, landmark premieres and history-making moments, featuring a Betsy Jolas debut inspired by Shakespeare's Tempest, music from the Spanish National Orchestra, both recorded this season, soprano Angel Blue's triumphant proms debut, and the first accordion soloist to grace the Last Night of the Proms stage - Ksenija Sidorova - transports us to the streets of Buenos Aires with her rendition of Piazzolla's Libertango.

programme.title: Bill Oddie Goes Wild
programme.desc: On his home patch of Hampstead Heath in London, Bill Oddie reminisces about his past travels in search of the best of British wildlife. We join him as he muses over some of his most memorable moments, and revisit some of his highlights, low points and outtakes from the past three series.

programme.title: Birding with Bill Oddie
programme.desc: In his practical guide to birdwatching and learning about birds, Bill Oddie revisits his childhood birding haunts to discover how they have changed over 50 years. Bill's first encounter with birds was when he was about seven years old. He found a dunnock's nest with five eggs in - he took one, put it in a matchbox and carefully put it in his back pocket. He then forgot about it, and later, when jumping over a log, crushed it. Egg-collecting is no longer legal, but it did teach him a lesson or two - it got him hooked on birds and taught him the value of patience.

programme.title: The Architecture the Railways Built

programme.title: The Flying Gardener
programme.desc: Series in which Chris Beardshaw visits inspirational gardens by helicopter. Featuring a trip to Britain's largest protected wetland to see some of Britain's rarest plants, and a look at some ponds filled with exotics.

programme.title: Art of Spain
programme.desc: Andrew Graham-Dixon reveals how northern Spain has produced some of the most dazzling and iconic art of the modern age. He shows how Spain's turbulent history has shaped its artists, from Francisco Goya and Pablo Picasso to Joan Miro and Salvador Dali. As well as the giants of painting, Graham-Dixon argues that Spanish architecture is the art form taking the nation forward into the new millennium.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Magnus Magnusson hosts from Reading University. Specialist subjects include PG Wodehouse, Vincent van Gogh, science fiction and John Buchan.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Robert Robinson chairs as team captains Frank Muir and Patrick Campbell are joined by André Previn, Tom Conti, Barbara Kellerman and Tina Brown.

programme.title: Art on the BBC
programme.desc: Michelangelo was not merely a giant of the Renaissance. He was also one of the era’s most controversial personalities. Art historian Sona Datta explores six decades of BBC archive to discover how TV has influenced our understanding of him. Sona reveals how TV has tried to reconcile Michelangelo’s art with his difficult personality, bringing to life the story of a man who rose from humble beginnings to become the favoured artist of the rich and powerful. He left us with work that was both iconic and divine, but his bitter, jealous temperament earned him more than a few enemies.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: Singer and writer George Melly takes a walk from his home in north London to the Hayward Gallery, reminiscing along the way about the influence of surrealism on his early life.

programme.title: Wainwright: The Man Who Loved the Lakes
programme.desc: Capturing the beauty of the English Lake District, a documentary which traces the life of writer and artist Alfred Wainwright, the eccentric Lancastrian who created a series of iconic fell-walking books which he hand-wrote, illustrated and published himself in the 1950s. Celebrating the centenary of his birth, the film captures his passionate love affair with the Lakeland landscape and explores how his books have become guide-book classics for millions of fell-walkers.

programme.title: Inside China's EV Revolution
programme.desc: At a time of heightened geopolitical conflict and uncertainty, soaring fuel costs are driving up demand for electric vehicles around the world. Chinese EV's are leading the way. In the span of a decade, China's electric vehicles sector has gone from fledgling industry to automotive powerhouse, challenging some the world's top automakers on their home ground. We examine how China transformed into the world's leading manufacturer of green energy cars, from innovations in battery technology to the concept of a smartphone on wheels, and ultimately what lies ahead for the future of transportation.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: In a series of four special programmes, John Craven explores the heritage of North Yorkshire. As the nation marks 200 years of the railway, John heads to the Wensleydale Railway – a much-loved line brought back to life by volunteers after decades of dereliction. John also delves into the programme's archives for a nostalgic look at the many ways we’ve travelled across the UK over the years.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee Burkhill and Amelia Bouquet are in Liverpool to transform Letrice and Andrew’s lacklustre plot into a wildflower meadow. Letrice wants to wander through tall grasses and prairie planting, while Andrew would like a man cave at the end of the garden. Can the team achieve all this on a £4,500 budget?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Jacqui gets that sinking feeling as she tours a Norwich house suffering from subsidence, while Martin is really surprised by developers' plans to rip everything out of a six-bedroom house in Cardiff, including the floors and staircase. There are also ambitious plans for a four-bedroom terrace in Dover.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Now you see it, now you don’t. Artist Martin Frost reveals the art of vanishing fore-edge painting. Martin is one of only a few people left creating artwork on the gilded sides of books, a craft that began all the way back in the 1660s. Hoping to make a few artful deals are nan and grandson Sheila and Frankie, who are shopping at Ardingly antiques fair with expert Caroline Hawley. Up against them are grandad and granddaughter Jeff and Sophie, guided by Thomas Forrester. Jeff plans to make a timely purchase at a stall of clocks, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a great way to tick off their challenge. Across the fair, a cast-iron umbrella stand, decorated with a dog under a tree, makes Sheila ‘paws’ for thought – until Caroline points out the three-figure price tag. In Chichester, Nick Hall is on the rostrum to hopefully hammer out profits for the teams. The reds pin their hopes on Thomas’s bonus buy, while Caroline causes a stir when she reveals hers.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Buckinghamshire, Jacqui Joseph explores Beaconsfield recycling centre determined to save quality items from being crushed. A 'beast' of a bookcase poses a huge challenge for carpenter Sam, while screen printer Zoe completely overhauls a tired cabinet. Jacqui spots potential in an unwanted footstool, but will a patchwork redesign produce profits?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In Aberdeenshire, Alistair Appleton helps Sonya and her son William find a country home with enough land for the whole family, including their ponies and horses. The search uncovers some fantastic properties, including an epically vast mystery house with enough bedrooms for the whole family as well as 17 guests to each enjoy one of their own! Along the way, Alistair meets influencer Aimee, a seasoned global explorer, who along with her partner has chosen to put down roots in rural Scotland by restoring their very own cottage.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: Childhood memories are restored alongside items such as a storybook made by two loving parents and a tweed flat cap that belonged to a bricklaying father who died far too young.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: The Child Maintenance Service is meant to make sure that parents who live apart from their children make regular payments to support them. But it stands accused of doing too little to enforce payments in some cases, leaving parents missing out on money they are legally entitled to, to help care for their children. Meanwhile, parents who make payments say calculations done by the CMS can sometimes be wrong or unaffordable, and that mistakes can affect their mental health. The government says it takes seriously the small number of cases where things go wrong and is making further improvements to the service. Reporter Krupa Padhy meets parents who receive maintenance and those who pay it, and asks whether the system is failing both them and their children?

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: In this episode, the team can not only hear a group of Lahore-based scammers, they can see them as well, as ethical hacker Jim Browning has broken into their CCTV system. And as the team look, open-mouthed, at an office full of scammers hard at work, one fraudster reels in a man in London who thinks that he is about to get a discounted mobile phone deal. In fact, he is on the hook for hundreds of pounds unless we can get hold of him. Meanwhile, in Liverpool, a different group of scammers try to convince a man that he has problems with his broadband and needs to give them access to his system to sort it out.

programme.title: Death in Paradise
programme.desc: A reggae rap artist is shot dead at a soundcheck for a concert. Things prove uncomfortable for Marlon when he discovers a personal connection to the crime.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Now you see it, now you don’t. Artist Martin Frost reveals the art of vanishing fore-edge painting. Martin is one of only a few people left creating artwork on the gilded sides of books, a craft that began all the way back in the 1660s. Hoping to make a few artful deals are nan and grandson Sheila and Frankie, who are shopping at Ardingly antiques fair with expert Caroline Hawley. Up against them are grandad and granddaughter Jeff and Sophie, guided by Thomas Forrester. Jeff plans to make a timely purchase at a stall of clocks, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a great way to tick off their challenge. Across the fair, a cast-iron umbrella stand, decorated with a dog under a tree, makes Sheila ‘paws’ for thought – until Caroline points out the three-figure price tag. In Chichester, Nick Hall is on the rostrum to hopefully hammer out profits for the teams. The reds pin their hopes on Thomas’s bonus buy, while Caroline causes a stir when she reveals hers.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: The Child Maintenance Service is meant to make sure that parents who live apart from their children make regular payments to support them. But it stands accused of doing too little to enforce payments in some cases, leaving parents missing out on money they are legally entitled to, to help care for their children. Meanwhile, parents who make payments say calculations done by the CMS can sometimes be wrong or unaffordable, and that mistakes can affect their mental health. The government says it takes seriously the small number of cases where things go wrong and is making further improvements to the service. Reporter Krupa Padhy meets parents who receive maintenance and those who pay it, and asks whether the system is failing both them and their children?

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: In this episode, the team can not only hear a group of Lahore-based scammers, they can see them as well, as ethical hacker Jim Browning has broken into their CCTV system. And as the team look, open-mouthed, at an office full of scammers hard at work, one fraudster reels in a man in London who thinks that he is about to get a discounted mobile phone deal. In fact, he is on the hook for hundreds of pounds unless we can get hold of him. Meanwhile, in Liverpool, a different group of scammers try to convince a man that he has problems with his broadband and needs to give them access to his system to sort it out.

programme.title: Girl Fight
programme.desc: At Next Generation gym in Ballymena, fighters train with grit and ambition under head coach Rodney Moore, who’s determined to shape champions from everyday people. Rachel ‘The Diva’ McIlhagga is one of them. An amateur kickboxer still reeling from a devastating MMA defeat, she’s struggled with self-belief ever since. Now, she’s preparing for a kickboxing bout in Dublin – a chance to reset, rebuild and prove she still has what it takes. Twenty-two-year-old Niamh McNeill is also a dedicated member of the gym, alongside her mum Julie. The two have trained side by side for nine years, and now they’re chasing a shared dream: to fight on the same card before Niamh leaves for a new life in Australia. Meanwhile, Chloe Crozier is preparing for the biggest bout of her career – her first title fight. Winning a title is an essential step towards a professional fighting career, so Chloe must win to keep her dream of turning pro alive.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: In a series of four special programmes, John Craven explores the heritage of North Yorkshire. As the nation marks 200 years of the railway, John heads to the Wensleydale Railway – a much-loved line brought back to life by volunteers after decades of dereliction. John also delves into the programme's archives for a nostalgic look at the many ways we’ve travelled across the UK over the years.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee Burkhill and Amelia Bouquet are in Liverpool to transform Letrice and Andrew’s lacklustre plot into a wildflower meadow. Letrice wants to wander through tall grasses and prairie planting, while Andrew would like a man cave at the end of the garden. Can the team achieve all this on a £4,500 budget?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Jacqui gets that sinking feeling as she tours a Norwich house suffering from subsidence, while Martin is really surprised by developers' plans to rip everything out of a six-bedroom house in Cardiff, including the floors and staircase. There are also ambitious plans for a four-bedroom terrace in Dover.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Now you see it, now you don’t. Artist Martin Frost reveals the art of vanishing fore-edge painting. Martin is one of only a few people left creating artwork on the gilded sides of books, a craft that began all the way back in the 1660s. Hoping to make a few artful deals are nan and grandson Sheila and Frankie, who are shopping at Ardingly antiques fair with expert Caroline Hawley. Up against them are grandad and granddaughter Jeff and Sophie, guided by Thomas Forrester. Jeff plans to make a timely purchase at a stall of clocks, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a great way to tick off their challenge. Across the fair, a cast-iron umbrella stand, decorated with a dog under a tree, makes Sheila ‘paws’ for thought – until Caroline points out the three-figure price tag. In Chichester, Nick Hall is on the rostrum to hopefully hammer out profits for the teams. The reds pin their hopes on Thomas’s bonus buy, while Caroline causes a stir when she reveals hers.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Buckinghamshire, Jacqui Joseph explores Beaconsfield recycling centre determined to save quality items from being crushed. A 'beast' of a bookcase poses a huge challenge for carpenter Sam, while screen printer Zoe completely overhauls a tired cabinet. Jacqui spots potential in an unwanted footstool, but will a patchwork redesign produce profits?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In Aberdeenshire, Alistair Appleton helps Sonya and her son William find a country home with enough land for the whole family, including their ponies and horses. The search uncovers some fantastic properties, including an epically vast mystery house with enough bedrooms for the whole family as well as 17 guests to each enjoy one of their own! Along the way, Alistair meets influencer Aimee, a seasoned global explorer, who along with her partner has chosen to put down roots in rural Scotland by restoring their very own cottage.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: Childhood memories are restored alongside items such as a storybook made by two loving parents and a tweed flat cap that belonged to a bricklaying father who died far too young.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Olivia Rodrigo or Sabrina Carpenter? Wales or Iceland? 1980s sport or 1990s sport? Jason Manford asks the questions, but will the teams pick the right answer?

programme.title: EastEnders

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: The Child Maintenance Service is meant to make sure that parents who live apart from their children make regular payments to support them. But it stands accused of doing too little to enforce payments in some cases, leaving parents missing out on money they are legally entitled to, to help care for their children. Meanwhile, parents who make payments say calculations done by the CMS can sometimes be wrong or unaffordable, and that mistakes can affect their mental health. The government says it takes seriously the small number of cases where things go wrong and is making further improvements to the service. Reporter Krupa Padhy meets parents who receive maintenance and those who pay it, and asks whether the system is failing both them and their children?

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: In this episode, the team can not only hear a group of Lahore-based scammers, they can see them as well, as ethical hacker Jim Browning has broken into their CCTV system. And as the team look, open-mouthed, at an office full of scammers hard at work, one fraudster reels in a man in London who thinks that he is about to get a discounted mobile phone deal. In fact, he is on the hook for hundreds of pounds unless we can get hold of him. Meanwhile, in Liverpool, a different group of scammers try to convince a man that he has problems with his broadband and needs to give them access to his system to sort it out.

programme.title: Disclosure
programme.desc: Disclosure investigates claims that parts of Scotland’s biggest city have become a 'no-go zone' because of crime, homelessness and antisocial behaviour. As thousands of tourists arrive in Glasgow for the summer, Myles Bonnar spends a week in the city centre exploring what might await them as they step off the train. Has disorder in the city become worse, or is tension simply being stoked online by those who trace every problem back to immigration?

Martin is one of only a few people left creating artwork on the gilded sides of books, a craft that began all the way back in the 1660s. Hoping to make a few artful deals are nan and grandson Sheila and Frankie, who are shopping at Ardingly antiques fair with expert Caroline Hawley. Up against them are grandad and granddaughter Jeff and Sophie, guided by Thomas Forrester. Jeff plans to make a timely purchase at a stall of clocks, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a great way to tick off their challenge. Across the fair, a cast-iron umbrella stand, decorated with a dog under a tree, makes Sheila ‘paws’ for thought – until Caroline points out the three-figure price tag. In Chichester, Nick Hall is on the rostrum to hopefully hammer out profits for the teams. The reds pin their hopes on Thomas’s bonus buy, while Caroline causes a stir when she reveals hers.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: The Child Maintenance Service is meant to make sure that parents who live apart from their children make regular payments to support them. But it stands accused of doing too little to enforce payments in some cases, leaving parents missing out on money they are legally entitled to, to help care for their children. Meanwhile, parents who make payments say calculations done by the CMS can sometimes be wrong or unaffordable, and that mistakes can affect their mental health. The government says it takes seriously the small number of cases where things go wrong and is making further improvements to the service. Reporter Krupa Padhy meets parents who receive maintenance and those who pay it, and asks whether the system is failing both them and their children?

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: In this episode, the team can not only hear a group of Lahore-based scammers, they can see them as well, as ethical hacker Jim Browning has broken into their CCTV system. And as the team look, open-mouthed, at an office full of scammers hard at work, one fraudster reels in a man in London who thinks that he is about to get a discounted mobile phone deal. In fact, he is on the hook for hundreds of pounds unless we can get hold of him. Meanwhile, in Liverpool, a different group of scammers try to convince a man that he has problems with his broadband and needs to give them access to his system to sort it out.

As the nation marks 200 years of the railway, John heads to the Wensleydale Railway – a much-loved line brought back to life by volunteers after decades of dereliction. John also delves into the programme's archives for a nostalgic look at the many ways we’ve travelled across the UK over the years.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Lee Burkhill and Amelia Bouquet are in Liverpool to transform Letrice and Andrew’s lacklustre plot into a wildflower meadow. Letrice wants to wander through tall grasses and prairie planting, while Andrew would like a man cave at the end of the garden. Can the team achieve all this on a £4,500 budget?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Jacqui gets that sinking feeling as she tours a Norwich house suffering from subsidence, while Martin is really surprised by developers' plans to rip everything out of a six-bedroom house in Cardiff, including the floors and staircase. There are also ambitious plans for a four-bedroom terrace in Dover.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Now you see it, now you don’t. Artist Martin Frost reveals the art of vanishing fore-edge painting. Martin is one of only a few people left creating artwork on the gilded sides of books, a craft that began all the way back in the 1660s. Hoping to make a few artful deals are nan and grandson Sheila and Frankie, who are shopping at Ardingly antiques fair with expert Caroline Hawley. Up against them are grandad and granddaughter Jeff and Sophie, guided by Thomas Forrester. Jeff plans to make a timely purchase at a stall of clocks, but Thomas doesn’t think it’s a great way to tick off their challenge. Across the fair, a cast-iron umbrella stand, decorated with a dog under a tree, makes Sheila ‘paws’ for thought – until Caroline points out the three-figure price tag. In Chichester, Nick Hall is on the rostrum to hopefully hammer out profits for the teams. The reds pin their hopes on Thomas’s bonus buy, while Caroline causes a stir when she reveals hers.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Buckinghamshire, Jacqui Joseph explores Beaconsfield recycling centre determined to save quality items from being crushed. A 'beast' of a bookcase poses a huge challenge for carpenter Sam, while screen printer Zoe completely overhauls a tired cabinet. Jacqui spots potential in an unwanted footstool, but will a patchwork redesign produce profits?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In Aberdeenshire, Alistair Appleton helps Sonya and her son William find a country home with enough land for the whole family, including their ponies and horses. The search uncovers some fantastic properties, including an epically vast mystery house with enough bedrooms for the whole family as well as 17 guests to each enjoy one of their own! Along the way, Alistair meets influencer Aimee, a seasoned global explorer, who along with her partner has chosen to put down roots in rural Scotland by restoring their very own cottage.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: Childhood memories are restored alongside items such as a storybook made by two loving parents and a tweed flat cap that belonged to a bricklaying father who died far too young.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Olivia Rodrigo or Sabrina Carpenter? Wales or Iceland? 1980s sport or 1990s sport? Jason Manford asks the questions, but will the teams pick the right answer?

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Nish Kumar for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: The One Show

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: A situation escalates for Nicola and George, Avani attempts to play matchmaker, and Amy worries about recent events.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: The Child Maintenance Service is meant to make sure that parents who live apart from their children make regular payments to support them. But it stands accused of doing too little to enforce payments in some cases, leaving parents missing out on money they are legally entitled to, to help care for their children. Meanwhile, parents who make payments say calculations done by the CMS can sometimes be wrong or unaffordable, and that mistakes can affect their mental health. The government says it takes seriously the small number of cases where things go wrong and is making further improvements to the service. Reporter Krupa Padhy meets parents who receive maintenance and those who pay it, and asks whether the system is failing both them and their children?

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: In this episode, the team can not only hear a group of Lahore-based scammers, they can see them as well, as ethical hacker Jim Browning has broken into their CCTV system. And as the team look, open-mouthed, at an office full of scammers hard at work, one fraudster reels in a man in London who thinks that he is about to get a discounted mobile phone deal. In fact, he is on the hook for hundreds of pounds unless we can get hold of him. Meanwhile, in Liverpool, a different group of scammers try to convince a man that he has problems with his broadband and needs to give them access to his system to sort it out.

programme.title: Death in Paradise
programme.desc: A reggae rap artist is shot dead at a soundcheck for a concert. Things prove uncomfortable for Marlon when he discovers a personal connection to the crime.

programme.title: The Mountain
programme.desc: The summer months bring new opportunities for the hardy folk who live in the shadow of Cairngorm. Perhaps the UK's weirdest music festival gets under way, the sailing school calls up new management to survive, and the ski patrol team takes on the adventure triathalon.

programme.title: Race Against the Tide
programme.desc: The sand-sculpting competition kicks off on St Andrews Beach as seven teams race to create seaside-inspired masterpieces in just six hours, before the tide sweeps in. From nostalgic caravans to cheeky seagulls, creativity meets chaos under the watchful eyes of judges Sadie and Jamie. Who will wow and who will wash out in this high-stakes battle against nature?

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: It's the semi-finals, and the three remaining designers head to Brighton and Hove Albion's football stadium to transform two hospitality boxes each - one for a player's family and the other for a corporate client. Top fan Norman Cook, aka Fatboy Slim, pops in for a visit, alongside players Georginio Rutter and Fran Kirby. There is a lot to juggle in this tough challenge, and a place in the final at stake.

programme.title: River City
programme.desc: A scheming Caitlin takes a convenient opportunity to troll Scarlett further, with explosive consequences. While Tommy is in critical condition, a devastated Roisin confronts Gillian, Harry is furious to find out Alex has control of his empire, and Angus makes a surprise discovery.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: There's great excitement as Colin introduces the neighbours to his new partner Anne Marie. But the gang are quickly taken aback by her enthusiastic approach to the dinner party.

programme.desc: Conversation about Scotland’s biggest news stories, hosted by Martin Geissler.

programme.desc: Sitcom. General Randy Badger arrives from America on official duty. He enlists Gary and the boys, and instigates his own mission - to drink beer, see strippers and find his Scottish ancestors, the McBadgers. Hoo ya.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: The Special Operations Response Team are called to the scene of a mountain bike accident in a hilly patch of East Ayrshire woodland. The patient’s bike seat has broken, causing him a painful and potentially dangerous injury. SORT crewmates Pam and Rob must now figure out how to move the patient across difficult ground and into a waiting ambulance. Fortunately, they have their Wolverine all-terrain vehicle to hand. Based in a community of around 10,000 people, Buckie teammates Vicki and Elaine often encounter friends and acquaintances on their ambulance shifts. They treat Isabella, who is struggling with breathing difficulties caused by her COPD, and old school bus driver George, who is displaying the signs of a stroke.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: George Anderson and Brian Cunningham delve into the mailbox to tackle a host of viewers’ questions sent in from around the country. Even though we are well into the growing season, the pair start a major new project as they launch a makeover of a Beechgrove area known as the Crooked Garden. One of the first parts of that revamp is the creation of a stumpery, a growing technique based on an old tree and planted with a range of ferns. George has details on how to feed a cherry tree, Brian is back in the 8x6 greenhouse, and there is a visit to St Andrews Botanic Garden.

programme.title: This is BBC Scotland
programme.desc: Highlights from the BBC Scotland channel.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: Sportscene: Scottish Women's Premier League
programme.desc: Jane Lewis presents highlights from the weekend’s fixtures in the SWPL.

programme.title: The Mountain
programme.desc: The summer months bring new opportunities for the hardy folk who live in the shadow of Cairngorm. Perhaps the UK's weirdest music festival gets under way, the sailing school calls up new management to survive, and the ski patrol team takes on the adventure triathalon.

programme.title: Race Against the Tide
programme.desc: The sand-sculpting competition kicks off on St Andrews Beach as seven teams race to create seaside-inspired masterpieces in just six hours, before the tide sweeps in. From nostalgic caravans to cheeky seagulls, creativity meets chaos under the watchful eyes of judges Sadie and Jamie. Who will wow and who will wash out in this high-stakes battle against nature?

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: It's the semi-finals, and the three remaining designers head to Brighton and Hove Albion's football stadium to transform two hospitality boxes each - one for a player's family and the other for a corporate client. Top fan Norman Cook, aka Fatboy Slim, pops in for a visit, alongside players Georginio Rutter and Fran Kirby. There is a lot to juggle in this tough challenge, and a place in the final at stake.

programme.title: River City
programme.desc: A scheming Caitlin takes a convenient opportunity to troll Scarlett further, with explosive consequences. While Tommy is in critical condition, a devastated Roisin confronts Gillian, Harry is furious to find out Alex has control of his empire, and Angus makes a surprise discovery.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: There's great excitement as Colin introduces the neighbours to his new partner Anne Marie. But the gang are quickly taken aback by her enthusiastic approach to the dinner party.

programme.title: Scotcast
programme.desc: Conversation about Scotland’s biggest news stories, hosted by Martin Geissler.

programme.title: Gary: Tank Commander
programme.desc: Sitcom. General Randy Badger arrives from America on official duty. He enlists Gary and the boys, and instigates his own mission - to drink beer, see strippers and find his Scottish ancestors, the McBadgers. Hoo ya.

programme.title: This is BBC Scotland
programme.desc: Highlights from the BBC Scotland channel.

programme.title: Him & Her
programme.desc: Steve and Becky are doing their usual thing - staying in bed and just about to have sex. Their plans are scuppered, however, when Laura turns up panicking because her fiancé, Paul, has stayed out all night. Steve just wants Laura to leave, but has to cover for Paul. And neighbour Dan wants to get melons. And eat them with spoons.

programme.title: Him & Her
programme.desc: It's Steve's birthday, and everyone wants to go out and get plastered - except Steve. He's ill in bed. Or at least he tells his mum and everyone else he is. When Becky, Laura, Shelly and Paul can't persuade him to go out and celebrate, Steve stays in and - with a little help from Dan - makes very good use of his presents.

programme.title: Him & Her
programme.desc: Paul's son, Little Luke, is out of hospital, so he's having a fancy dress party to celebrate. Steve and Becky have to go, but they don't want to. Becky dithers over a spot on her chin. Steve can't get through to his bank. And when a furious Paul comes over to see why they're so late and what's happened to the sausage rolls, it seems they have no option but to go.

programme.title: Him & Her
programme.desc: Everyone is trying to watch the match between two local teams, except for Steve, who is bothered by a dream he had about Becky and her ex, Laura, who is bored, and Paul, who is miserable after his mum's shocking news. The afternoon couldn't really be going worse, until Steve comes out with what appears to be a racist comment.

programme.title: Him & Her
programme.desc: It's a Sunday and Becky and Steve are bored. Their fridge is broken, and Becky's parents are coming round to fix it. Steve has never met them before, and he's terrified. When they arrive, he's over-friendly and frankly a bit odd. Matters are only made worse by Dan, who is audibly enjoying himself upstairs with his new girlfriend, Paris. At least, he says she's his girlfriend.

programme.title: The Catch Up
programme.desc: A round-up of the day's news.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve and his trusty team head to the frozen north of Norway. He follows the tracks of Europe's largest cat, the elusive lynx, up into the hills in the hope of seeing one, and gets a little nervous when he meets some in captivity. Arctic foxes and musk oxen are also on the menu in this deadly snowy episode.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve and the Deadly 60 team are on their home turf, the UK. The adventure begins in a lake as Steve dives in to track down a deadly monster lurking in its depths. Then it's off to a wind tunnel to check out how eagles fly. Finally, Steve builds a giant web to demonstrate just what lethal killers spiders can be.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It's week 5, and the sewers are tackling the wide world of sport. In the Pattern Challenge, they hit the beach to create classic men’s swimming shorts. The Transformation Challenge sees yet another Sewing Bee first, as the remaining eight sewers are divided into pairs for the first ever team challenge: working together to create outfits from recycled windsurf sails. Finally, the sewers are aiming for a strike as they use free-motion embroidery and applique to personalise their made-to-measure bowling shirts.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Motoring show. Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May head to Italy for a supercar shootout featuring the Lamborghini Aventador, the McLaren MP4-12C and the Noble M600. Their trip starts at the incredible Nardo test track, a facility so massive it is visible from space, before heading north for a nerve-wracking drive around the centre of Rome. The journey concludes at the legendary Imola circuit, a track challenging enough to have embarrassed many an F1 driver, with a timed challenge against the incredible skills of the Stig. Back in the studio, the presenters look forward to some car highlights of 2012 and another top celebrity guest takes the wheel of the Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.desc: A journey home leads Professor Ryan away from the team. Harry and Leo recruit Nikki Alexander to the team.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: George Anderson and Brian Cunningham delve into the mailbox to tackle a host of viewers’ questions sent in from around the country. programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Blackadder or The Young Ones? Beef or Chicken? Today’s teams will need to stay sharp and trust their instincts as Jason Manford hosts the quiz where questions have just two possible answers.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: The team revive a cherished rocking horse, a spectacular set of conga drums, and a logbook that played a key role in British LGBTQ+ history.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Nina Conti, Nick Helm, Athena Kugblenu and Toby Tarrant take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: The competition kicks off in Belfast as Vernon Kay and unreliable tour guide Paul Gorton serve up facts, fibs and playful distractions as the celebrity players attempt to sort truth from twaddle. This week’s guests are presenter Owain Wyn Evans, Olympic champion Greg Rutherford and Blue Peter’s Abby Cook, and their competition kicks off in Belfast. A daily winner is declared at the end of each show, with scores building across the five days as the race to reveal the week's overall champion gets going.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Ben and Kate return to Longleat, where a lion needs surgery to amputate part of his tail. Kate gets a surprise with the eland babies, and Ben has a brush with a gorilla.

programme.title: Serengeti
programme.desc: There’s humour, heartbreak and nail-biting tension as our animal families face new tests and fresh rivalries. Soon a devastating storm creates the biggest problem of all.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel presents the show in which members of the public are invited to bring along their antiques for examination. At Renishaw Hall in Derbyshire, discoveries include a collection of swords, a homing pigeon clock, a patchwork quilt and a valuable painting of a lion.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the National Maritime Museum, Cornwall, based in Falmouth. Antiques expert Philip Serrell finds an unusual tortoise with an excellent pedigree and Caroline Hawley takes an electric guitar to auction which plucks at the heartstrings of the bidders. Presenter Paul Martin goes deep underground to uncover Cornwall's industrial past.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, former winners Edith Bowman, Rhys James, Anita Rani and Simon Rimmer take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall House of Champions winner being crowned on Friday. Will they opt for the House of Games golden cowboy hat, or instead go for the must-have golden wheelie luggage?

programme.title: Bear Grylls - Wild Reckoning
programme.desc: Yorkshire couple Julie and Jason were happily married for 27 years. However, five years ago, Julie started going through perimenopause and menopause, which changed everything. She had no idea why she suddenly felt so different about the relationship. The couple began constantly fighting, and she even left her husband on several occasions. Now she is getting the correct medical treatment for her symptoms, it’s time to repair the hurt caused by five years of hostility and unkindness. The couple take on a problem-solving challenge to see how they work together, before Bear sets them a rescue mission - to keep an ember alight while gathering fuel for a signal fire. Relationship therapist Simone talks to them about the hurt they have experienced and encourages them to rekindle the spark they once shared. Can they break the negative patterns they have fallen into? Or is it too late to undo the damage?

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. On this episode, Aleem Maqbool reports from Cape Coast, Ghana, on the country's efforts to spearhead a global campaign for reparations from nations and institutions that profited from the transatlantic slave trade. And BBC Eye has exclusive access to Interpol officers as they target human trafficking networks in West Africa and help a father search for his missing children.‌

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents another heat of the classic quiz, where contenders take on the famous black chair under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are Iron Maiden, Transport for London moquette, the films of Paul Newman and the Tintin books of Hergé.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. A high-scoring game, but since nobody goes home tonight, you could say it’s just for fun. And if your idea of fun is questions such as: what connects Gladiator Kim Betts, David Bowie, Pikachu and The Flash, then you’ve definitely come to the right place.

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: Teams from Bath and City St George’s University play their first game in the competition. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Buried with Michael Sheen
programme.desc: For years, Welsh actor Michael Sheen has been haunted by a story he discovered online about little-known farming consultant Douglas Gowan, who claimed the people of Wales had been poisoned by decades of toxic chemical dumping of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) - a known class 1 carcinogen often called the 'godfather of forever chemicals'. Unable to let the story go, Michael follows a toxic trail that leads him to ask: who’s in danger now?

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob set off in a punt to fish for perch on a weir pool on the River Thames - leaving poor old terrier Ted forlorn on the river bank, as he is not allowed on the boat with them. They discuss the treats we give ourselves in life, however simple they may be. The trio are also joined by comedian Richard Herring for a heart healthy meal.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Faisal Islam.

programme.title: Disclosure
programme.desc: Disclosure investigates claims that parts of Scotland’s biggest city have become a 'no-go zone' because of crime, homelessness and antisocial behaviour. As thousands of tourists arrive in Glasgow for the summer, Myles Bonnar spends a week in the city centre exploring what might await them as they step off the train. Has disorder in the city become worse, or is tension simply being stoked online by those who trace every problem back to immigration?

programme.title: A House Through Time
programme.desc: The house's first residents are the Rev William Fitzsimmons, an 18th-century Episcopal Church minister who is arrested for helping French prisoners escape from Edinburgh Castle; Francis and Isabella Ronaldson, the former a post office worker who spied on Glasgow weavers to detect signs of radicalism; and the Steell family, including John, a skilled craftsman but terrible businessman, and his son John Steell Junior, who became one of Edinburgh's finest sculptors.

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Sue wishes she could see the Leonids meteor storm one last time in her life under clear skies, so Linda persuades her to go camping. But Linda inadvertently causes chaos at the campsite, and things get worse when they decide to go for a walk to get away from their fellow campers. Meanwhile, Michael gets some life-changing news.

But Linda inadvertently causes chaos at the campsite, and things get worse when they decide to go for a walk to get away from their fellow campers. Meanwhile, Michael gets some life-changing news.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: George Anderson and Brian Cunningham delve into the mailbox to tackle a host of viewers’ questions sent in from around the country. Even though we are well into the growing season, the pair start a major new project as they launch a makeover of a Beechgrove area known as the Crooked Garden. One of the first parts of that revamp is the creation of a stumpery, a growing technique based on an old tree and planted with a range of ferns. George has details on how to feed a cherry tree, Brian is back in the 8x6 greenhouse, and there is a visit to St Andrews Botanic Garden.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Blackadder or The Young Ones? Beef or Chicken? Today’s teams will need to stay sharp and trust their instincts as Jason Manford hosts the quiz where questions have just two possible answers.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: The team revive a cherished rocking horse, a spectacular set of conga drums, and a logbook that played a key role in British LGBTQ+ history.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Nina Conti, Nick Helm, Athena Kugblenu and Toby Tarrant take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: The competition kicks off in Belfast as Vernon Kay and unreliable tour guide Paul Gorton serve up facts, fibs and playful distractions as the celebrity players attempt to sort truth from twaddle. This week’s guests are presenter Owain Wyn Evans, Olympic champion Greg Rutherford and Blue Peter’s Abby Cook, and their competition kicks off in Belfast. A daily winner is declared at the end of each show, with scores building across the five days as the race to reveal the week's overall champion gets going.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Ben and Kate return to Longleat, where a lion needs surgery to amputate part of his tail. Kate gets a surprise with the eland babies, and Ben has a brush with a gorilla.

programme.title: Serengeti
programme.desc: There’s humour, heartbreak and nail-biting tension as our animal families face new tests and fresh rivalries. Soon a devastating storm creates the biggest problem of all.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel presents the show in which members of the public are invited to bring along their antiques for examination. At Renishaw Hall in Derbyshire, discoveries include a collection of swords, a homing pigeon clock, a patchwork quilt and a valuable painting of a lion.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the National Maritime Museum, Cornwall, based in Falmouth. Antiques expert Philip Serrell finds an unusual tortoise with an excellent pedigree and Caroline Hawley takes an electric guitar to auction which plucks at the heartstrings of the bidders. Presenter Paul Martin goes deep underground to uncover Cornwall's industrial past.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, former winners Edith Bowman, Rhys James, Anita Rani and Simon Rimmer take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall House of Champions winner being crowned on Friday. Will they opt for the House of Games golden cowboy hat, or instead go for the must-have golden wheelie luggage?

programme.title: Bear Grylls - Wild Reckoning
programme.desc: Yorkshire couple Julie and Jason were happily married for 27 years. However, five years ago, Julie started going through perimenopause and menopause, which changed everything. She had no idea why she suddenly felt so different about the relationship. The couple began constantly fighting, and she even left her husband on several occasions. Now she is getting the correct medical treatment for her symptoms, it’s time to repair the hurt caused by five years of hostility and unkindness. The couple take on a problem-solving challenge to see how they work together, before Bear sets them a rescue mission - to keep an ember alight while gathering fuel for a signal fire. Relationship therapist Simone talks to them about the hurt they have experienced and encourages them to rekindle the spark they once shared. Can they break the negative patterns they have fallen into? Or is it too late to undo the damage?

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. On this episode, Aleem Maqbool reports from Cape Coast, Ghana, on the country's efforts to spearhead a global campaign for reparations from nations and institutions that profited from the transatlantic slave trade. And BBC Eye has exclusive access to Interpol officers as they target human trafficking networks in West Africa and help a father search for his missing children.‌

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents another heat of the classic quiz, where contenders take on the famous black chair under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are Iron Maiden, Transport for London moquette, the films of Paul Newman and the Tintin books of Hergé.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. A high-scoring game, but since nobody goes home tonight, you could say it’s just for fun. And if your idea of fun is questions such as: what connects Gladiator Kim Betts, David Bowie, Pikachu and The Flash, then you’ve definitely come to the right place.

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: Teams from Bath and City St George’s University play their first game in the competition. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Buried with Michael Sheen
programme.desc: For years, Welsh actor Michael Sheen has been haunted by a story he discovered online about little-known farming consultant Douglas Gowan, who claimed the people of Wales had been poisoned by decades of toxic chemical dumping of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) - a known class 1 carcinogen often called the 'godfather of forever chemicals'. Unable to let the story go, Michael follows a toxic trail that leads him to ask: who’s in danger now?

programme.title: Ar An Sliabh
programme.desc: Sa chéad eagrán, faigheann an dearthóir seodra, Brian inspioráid ó Chnoc Bhréanainn i gContae Chiarraí le píosaí galánta ealaíne a chruthú. Leanann John Joe le hobair a shinsir agus é ag feirmeoireacht ar thaobh an tsléibhe – ag cloí le cur chuige traidisiúnta ach ag fáiltiú roimh an nuálaíocht chomh maith. I nDún na nGall, láimhseálann Louise agus Domhnall an timaistear laethúil, cúrsaí oibre agus cúrsaí teaghlaigh ag bun na hEaragaile. I nGlinnte Aontroma, is bean ghnóthach í Deirdre, an tOifigeach Forbartha Gaeilge, agus í ag taisteal ar mhuir agus ar tír le Gaeilge a thabhairt don chéad ghlúin eile. In this episode, jewellery designer Brian draws inspiration from Kerry’s Mount Brandon to create beautiful works of art, while John Joe carries on the work of his ancestors as he farms the slopes, embracing both traditional and modern practices. In Donegal, Louise and Domhnall juggle daily commutes to work and family life at the foot of Errigal Mountain. In the Glens of Antrim, Irish language development officer Deirdre is a busy woman as she journeys up mountain and across sea to introduce the next generation to the language.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Faisal Islam.

programme.title: Disclosure
programme.desc: Disclosure investigates claims that parts of Scotland’s biggest city have become a 'no-go zone' because of crime, homelessness and antisocial behaviour. As thousands of tourists arrive in Glasgow for the summer, Myles Bonnar spends a week in the city centre exploring what might await them as they step off the train. Has disorder in the city become worse, or is tension simply being stoked online by those who trace every problem back to immigration?

programme.title: A House Through Time
programme.desc: The house's first residents are the Rev William Fitzsimmons, an 18th-century Episcopal Church minister who is arrested for helping French prisoners escape from Edinburgh Castle; Francis and Isabella Ronaldson, the former a post office worker who spied on Glasgow weavers to detect signs of radicalism; and the Steell family, including John, a skilled craftsman but terrible businessman, and his son John Steell Junior, who became one of Edinburgh's finest sculptors.

programme.desc: Paul and Bob set off in a punt to fish for perch on a weir pool on the River Thames - leaving poor old terrier Ted forlorn on the river bank, as he is not allowed on the boat with them. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: The competition kicks off in Belfast as Vernon Kay and unreliable tour guide Paul Gorton serve up facts, fibs and playful distractions as the celebrity players attempt to sort truth from twaddle. This week’s guests are presenter Owain Wyn Evans, Olympic champion Greg Rutherford and Blue Peter’s Abby Cook, and their competition kicks off in Belfast. A daily winner is declared at the end of each show, with scores building across the five days as the race to reveal the week's overall champion gets going.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Ben and Kate return to Longleat, where a lion needs surgery to amputate part of his tail. Kate gets a surprise with the eland babies, and Ben has a brush with a gorilla.

programme.title: Serengeti
programme.desc: There’s humour, heartbreak and nail-biting tension as our animal families face new tests and fresh rivalries. Soon a devastating storm creates the biggest problem of all.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel presents the show in which members of the public are invited to bring along their antiques for examination. At Renishaw Hall in Derbyshire, discoveries include a collection of swords, a homing pigeon clock, a patchwork quilt and a valuable painting of a lion.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the National Maritime Museum, Cornwall, based in Falmouth. Antiques expert Philip Serrell finds an unusual tortoise with an excellent pedigree and Caroline Hawley takes an electric guitar to auction which plucks at the heartstrings of the bidders. Presenter Paul Martin goes deep underground to uncover Cornwall's industrial past.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, former winners Edith Bowman, Rhys James, Anita Rani and Simon Rimmer take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall House of Champions winner being crowned on Friday. Will they opt for the House of Games golden cowboy hat, or instead go for the must-have golden wheelie luggage?

programme.title: Bear Grylls - Wild Reckoning
programme.desc: Yorkshire couple Julie and Jason were happily married for 27 years. However, five years ago, Julie started going through perimenopause and menopause, which changed everything. She had no idea why she suddenly felt so different about the relationship. The couple began constantly fighting, and she even left her husband on several occasions. Now she is getting the correct medical treatment for her symptoms, it’s time to repair the hurt caused by five years of hostility and unkindness. The couple take on a problem-solving challenge to see how they work together, before Bear sets them a rescue mission - to keep an ember alight while gathering fuel for a signal fire. Relationship therapist Simone talks to them about the hurt they have experienced and encourages them to rekindle the spark they once shared. Can they break the negative patterns they have fallen into? Or is it too late to undo the damage?

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. On this episode, Aleem Maqbool reports from Cape Coast, Ghana, on the country's efforts to spearhead a global campaign for reparations from nations and institutions that profited from the transatlantic slave trade. And BBC Eye has exclusive access to Interpol officers as they target human trafficking networks in West Africa and help a father search for his missing children.‌

programme.title: Mastermind

A high-scoring game, but since nobody goes home tonight, you could say it’s just for fun. programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘a’, and we go on an adventure around the sound. We see an astronaut, some adorable alpacas and an angry alligator! programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs can’t wait to watch the season finale of their favourite show, Trumpet Cat. But there’s one small problem… snack attacks! Maddie’s popcorn is loud, Triggs’s doggy biccies are even louder - and no-one can hear Trumpet Cat! As Maddie and Triggs grumble about how annoying and different the other one is, they also wonder if these differences might also be what makes them the perfect pair.

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: It's the hottest day of the year in Fine Forest. The Piggies build an ice machine for cold drinks. Wilf wants it all to himself - and accidentally causes a blizzard!

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos visit a hotel and find themselves hiding behind a line of suitcases. One by one, the porter takes each suitcase away, and the Twirlywoos move down the line, hiding behind different cases. When there is only one suitcase left, the Twirlywoos have nowhere else to hide. Instead of coming out from their hiding place, they take their hiding place with them, much to the porter's confusion! Back on the Big Red Boat, a mischievous mouse entertains on the Twirlywoo Screen. Where is he hiding?

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin and his friends visit the cinema to watch a very special funny film. Meanwhile, Mr Tumble directs his own film with a little help from all of his toys!

programme.title: Teletubbies

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Giovanna and Baby Bear welcome babies Tobias, Inam, Isaac, Enya, Hawa, Jean and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities, too! Inside everyone’s bags are shakers and rattles which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding baby appropriate shaker or rattle inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun song ‘Dingle Dangle Scarecrow’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Together Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: I Spy, You Spy
programme.desc: Elsee plays I-spy in the hair salon with her new friend Royalty.

programme.title: What’s in Your Plant Pot?
programme.desc: Worm farmer Heather and the Fact Pack get hands-on with wiggly worms! We learn how wonderful worms help plants grow.

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk to an old castle. On the way, they explore the rocky beach, go through a magic archway, walk like crabs and even see a pirate!

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Lou invents a new kind of race in which the slowest is the winner.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and Bingo don’t want to tidy the playroom, so they get Daddy Robot to do it for them. But when Bluey takes things too far, Daddy Robot malfunctions – with disastrous results.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are off for a jamboree to make some new friends, play games and have a picnic. They meet another group of young animals with their very own version of Duggee, but everything they do is different - even Roly finds one of them too LOUD!

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: An excitable Red arrives in Colourland. Learn about the colour red with the Colourblocks.

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures

Also, we find out how ants play an important role in the growing of plants and crops. They are amazing soil engineers!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Mum and Dad have a treat in store for George and Freddie. It’s a special tennis game including dinosaurs, bees, and smiley faces. But will they score an ace? Later, George and Freddie get the face paints out and transform Mum and Dad into colourful cats. What will they think of their amazing makeovers?

programme.title: Big Cook Little Cook
programme.desc: Small is entering the local talent show, but she’s forgotten the words to her song. Meanwhile, Mike the music man comes to visit, Small flies off to see how celery grows, and the two chefs serve a delicious risotto drum to their talented guest.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: When guide dog Kika has a waggy tail-related accident with a purple smoothie, she and her owner Dr Amit visit the Woofton Library of Things to borrow a carpet cleaner.

programme.title: Time for School
programme.desc: It’s the start of a new day, and Wren has made a card for her best friend Emmy. Outside, Wren, Emmy and Ayat discover a ladybird, which soon flies away. They go in search of their new fluttery friend, but will they be able to find it? Later, it’s Solomon’s turn to sit at the VIP table as he has been doing so well at school, and he chooses Lusungu as his guest. Finally, Sophie has a fun activity for Wren, Solomon and Lusungu - they are going on a pretend train trip in search of dinosaurs.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle won’t move from his new doggy doormat because he loves it very much. Jess opens the door to reveal Gram and Grand have come to visit and Grand has made coconut cake for everyone plus a special cake for Waffle but Waffle won’t move from his doggy door mat to greet him. Gram and Grand discover that Waffle can talk and Evie tells them Waffle’s learning to read, too. Gram gives Waffle a congratulatory snuggle and Waffle loves it!

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Mama and Papa are taking Oona and Baba on a family outing to experience something special - Papa tells them it's a big surprise. Oona and Baba are very excited to see it, but they need to find the perfect spot - which isn't easy. In the end, the amazing surprise makes all of their effort worth it.

programme.title: Yukee

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Fred and Dana ask the Piggies to plan fun outdoor games for Keith and Rebecca. Each piggy comes up with an idea, but Cesar’s is so ambitious that he can’t tackle it alone!

programme.title: Molly and Mack
programme.desc: Molly examines her shelf of special things at the back of Mack’s stall. She chooses the wobbly coffee pot mug and remembers the day she got it. Moira reads a bad online review of the Big Hub and worries that if word gets out, it will have to close. The review describes Kez’s stall as messy, so Moira decides to hold a stall inspection to sort things out. Although Molly loves the creative chaos of Kez’s stall, she agrees to help Kez tidy up before the inspection. Moira arrives for her inspection of Kez’s stall, and despite the stall being spotless, one Hub rule is broken, so Kez’s stall must close for the day. Meanwhile, Molly has an idea which could help Kez. As Moira inspects all the other stalls, she finds the same rule has been broken by everyone, including herself. Molly helps Moira realise that, unless she wants to close down all the stalls, she will have to rethink some of her rules.

programme.desc: It is Tag's birthday and Duggee has put up a bouncy castle to celebrate. It's a lovely sunny day, and the squirrels are all excited. They are just about to get bouncing when a big, gloomy cloud settles down and falls asleep right over the bouncy castle. How can they wake it up? Well, they could bounce up and tell it to move. Is this something Hedgley the hedgehog can help them with?

Lusungu finds that opening yogurt lids can be a bit tricky. Luckily, Mrs Farrell is on hand to help. The day continues as Silas and Maily create family portraits. Silas has fun drawing his mum's, but finds it harder to draw his pet cats - so he draws rabbits instead!

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Supertato, Carrot and Tomato are making friendship bracelets in the craft aisle, but this gives Evil Pea the crafty idea of making a monster costume to scare them all out of the supermarket. With herself and the Corn Cobs stacked on top of each other, they initially get the veggies to run away. Supertato wonders if the monster is just looking for a new friend, so he chases after it! When one of the arms falls off the monster, the Tato Team realise it’s just someone in a costume. They find out it was Evil Pea all along!

programme.desc: Rafi wants her dads to stop doing chores and to dance with her. She wishes to be the oldest so that she can set the rules. Suddenly, Jake and Dash turn into babies, leaving Rafi in charge! It’s funny at first, but soon the mess grows. Rafi realises being a grown-up means taking responsibility. She cleverly mixes tidying with dancing, showing them chores can be fun too. When the wish ends, her dads return to normal and are proud of Rafi’s maturity and teamwork.

programme.desc: JoJo is having a summer sleepover at Gran Gran's house and has brought everything she needs from home, including her favourite bedtime storybook. JoJo wanted to see the twinkly sleepover stars before she slept, just like the ones on the cover of her storybook. Gran Gran resolves to use fairy lights to create their own night time starry sky, and JoJo learns that the sun stays in the sky longer during summer.
